sources.retrosheet: Retrosheet parsed play files, regular season 2023, 2024, 2025. The information used here was obtained free of charge from and is copyrighted by Retrosheet. Interested parties may contact Retrosheet at www.retrosheet.org.
sources.savant: Baseball Savant sprint speed and outfield arm strength leaderboards (MLB Advanced Media), 2023, 2024, 2025.
sources.statsapi: MLB Stats API season stolen-base and caught-stealing totals (MLB Advanced Media), joined to sprint speed by MLBAM id.

batterTiers.note: Tiers by the batter's own season in the same data: weak = bottom quarter of OPS (PA-weighted, 150+ PA), strong = top quarter.

infield_in_usage.why: Public data never records a drawn-in infield (Statcast's alignment field has no infield-in category). What it does show: with a runner on third and fewer than two outs, ground balls, line drives and bloop flies fall for hits more often than in the same base state with two outs, when the infield always plays back. The drawn-in effect on each batted-ball type is that observed difference divided by how often infields are actually in — this one assumption. With 55% the defaults also reproduce the one-out ground-ball mix (runner scores on ~40% of outs, thrown out at home on ~19%).

infield_back_score_on_gb_out.why: With the infield back and fewer than two outs, share of ground-ball outs on which the runner from third scores (runner going on contact, play made at first).

infield_in_score_on_gb_out.why: With the infield in, share of ground-ball outs on which the runner from third still scores (slow rollers, balls to the side).

infield_out_at_home.why: Share of ground-ball outs that become a fielder's choice at home (runner out, batter safe at first): common with the infield in, rare with it back.

bunt_fail.why: Retrosheet records bunts put in play; attempts that are fouled off or missed until the batter must swing are invisible in it. This share of bunt attempts is treated as an out without advancing the runner, so the bunt isn't credited with only its successful tries.

throw_miss.why: Share of throws home that are off-line, cut off, bobbled or not cleanly applied, so the runner is safe whatever the timing. Keeps the timing model from treating any send as certain.

corners_in_share.why: Corners in / middle back applies the drawn-in effect only to balls hit to the corner infielders (and pitcher); the middle infielders play back. Share of the full effect on those balls.

steal_catcher_effect.why: Change in steal success for a strong (−) or weak (+) throwing catcher / quick-to-the-plate pitcher combination versus average. The speed effect is fitted; battery effects are not (they need per-attempt pop times).

charging_time.why: Seconds saved by an outfielder charging hard on a single compared with an average approach.

send_timing.why: Geometry of a throw home from the outfield (fielding distance by depth, release and tag time, throw carry); constants below, fitted offset and spread under fits.send2.

send1_timing.why: A runner from first on a double: the ball is played off the wall or in the gap and relayed home (outfielder to cutoff man to catcher). Constants below, fitted offset and spread under fits.send1.

tag_timing.why: Catch-and-throw geometry on a fly ball with a runner tagging at third; constants below, fitted offset and spread under fits.tag3.

send2.fittedOn: two-out singles with a runner on second (coaches near break-even)

send1.fittedOn: two-out doubles with a runner on first only (coaches near break-even)

tag3.fittedOn: fly balls caught by an outfielder with a runner on third and fewer than two outs
